data.name: Legal_Privacy_Intro
data.value: Hi, I'm Adrian. I built CircleTools for my own family, and I treat your data the way I'd want mine treated: I keep as little of it as I can. Secret Santa works offline and without an account. You only need one if you want to sync across your devices or use Circles. Here's what happens to your data, in plain words. (Legally, this follows the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection, the FADP, and the EU's GDPR where it applies.)

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ControllerBody
data.value: Just me: Adrian Moll. I'm a software engineer and build CircleTools (circletools.ch) in my free time. If you ever have a question about your data, write to me at info@circletools.ch and I'll answer.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_DataBody
data.value: If you create an account, I store your email address, the display name you choose, your language and your password — never as you typed it, only in a coded form that can't be turned back into your password. If you use a passkey, I keep only its public part. For each device you're signed in on, I store a rough label such as "Firefox on Windows" and when it was last active, so you can see your sign-ins under Security and end them. To make shared groups and Circles work, I store what you put in them: names, wishlists, event details and the assignments a draw produces. I don't ask for your birthday, your address, your phone number or any payment details. Email addresses that are only used to match an invitation are stored in the same coded form, never in plain text. The one exception is sending an email: so it can be delivered, the address is held briefly in plain text and deleted at the latest 7 days after sending.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LocalFirstHeading
data.value: Without an account, your data stays on your device

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LocalFirstBody
data.value: If you don't create an account, everything you set up stays on your own device — in your browser or in the app on your phone — and never reaches me. For these groups, the assignment is inside the reveal link itself, so opening one doesn't send me anything either. The app you use to send a link — WhatsApp, email or anything else — can see it, though, just like any other message. Only what you choose reaches my servers: if you put a group online so others can take part, it's stored with me; and if you open someone else's online group through their link, you're using the group that's already there.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_OthersBody
data.value: In a group you enter other people too: their names, maybe their wishlists and, if the whole family takes part, children's names as well. Please only add people who'd be happy with that, and remove them if they ask you to. Anyone who wants their data removed and can't reach you can write to me at info@circletools.ch.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LegalBasisHeading
data.value: Why I'm allowed to handle it

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LegalBasisBody
data.value: I use your account and what you enter so the app can do what you asked it to. Reminders are notifications on your own phone: they're off until you switch them on, and they never go through my servers. The only thing I do without asking is keep the app secure and stop abuse.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ProcessorsHeading
data.value: Where your data lives, and who helps me

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ProcessorsBody
data.value: Your account and your online groups are stored on servers at Infomaniak in Geneva, Switzerland. The encrypted backups are with Infomaniak too, on Swiss Backup in Switzerland. Emails go out through Brevo, a provider in the EU (France). The app only sends emails about your account or an invitation: confirming your address, changes to your password or address, security notices, invitations, and a short confirmation when you delete your account. No newsletters, no advertising. Apart from those emails, your data stays in Switzerland, and both companies only act on my instructions. If you install the app from Google Play or the App Store, Google or Apple handle that download under their own privacy policies; the app itself contains no code from them for tracking or advertising.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LogsBody
data.value: Like any server, mine writes technical logs — for example when an error happens. I use them only to keep the app running and to find bugs. They stay on my server in Switzerland, aren't passed on to anyone, and are deleted after 30 days. Your IP address is only used for a moment to slow down repeated attempts, for example at sign-in, and isn't stored.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_RetentionBody
data.value: An account you sign up for but never confirm is deleted after 30 days. If you don't use the app on a device for 30 days, you're signed out there automatically; resetting your password or deleting your account signs you out everywhere. An invitation to a Circle expires after 14 days, an invitation to a Secret Santa group after 30 days, and either is deleted as soon as it's accepted, declined or expires. Emails are deleted from my server at the latest 7 days after sending. A group kept online that no account owns is removed after a year without any activity. When you delete your account, it's gone from the app straight away and for good. The only copy left is in my encrypted backups, where it can stay for up to about six months before it's deleted for good.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_RightsBody
data.value: You can see, correct, download and delete your data whenever you like. Download and delete are right in the app: open the account menu at the top right (your initial) and choose "Data & account" — no request, no waiting. The download is a file (JSON) with everything your account holds on my servers; what's only on your device isn't in it, because you already have it. If something's on your mind, just email me at info@circletools.ch. And if you ever feel I've mishandled your data, you can turn to the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) or the data-protection authority where you live.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_CookiesBody
data.value: The app only stores what it needs on your device: your groups (if you keep them there), your sign-in and your settings. No advertising cookies, no third-party trackers, no profiling — none of that, ever.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ChangesBody
data.value: If the app grows and this page needs to change, I'll update it right here. The date at the top always shows the current version.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_OperatorBody
data.value: CircleTools is run by me, Adrian Moll (circletools.ch). The easiest way to reach me is info@circletools.ch.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_HostingBody
data.value: The app itself runs on your phone or in your browser. The database and the backend service behind it, which hold your account and your online groups, run on servers at Infomaniak in Geneva, Switzerland.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_DisclaimerBody
data.value: I build CircleTools with care, but it's a free personal project: I can't promise it will always work perfectly or always be available, and as far as the law allows, I can't accept liability for problems that come from using it. I'm not responsible for the content of other websites I link to.

data.name: Legal_Delete_Intro
data.value: This page explains how to remove your data from Secret Santa and your CircleTools account. I'm Adrian Moll, and I run CircleTools. Your data is yours, and you can leave at any time: delete your whole account, single things inside it, or what's kept only on your device.

data.name: Legal_Delete_InAppBody
data.value: Sign in, open the account menu at the top right (your initial) and choose "Data & account". Under "Delete account", enter your password and choose "Delete my account". It happens straight away and for good: your profile, your Circle memberships and the invitations you sent are deleted, and you leave every group you take part in. If you organise online groups, you choose once for all of them: delete them too, or keep them online so everyone taking part keeps access.

data.name: Legal_Delete_PartialHeading
data.value: Deleting single things and keeping your account

data.name: Legal_Delete_PartialBody
data.value: You can also delete just some things and keep your account. On the Groups screen, open a group's menu and choose "Delete" to remove the group and everything in it, or "Leave group" for a group you only take part in. Inside a group, open an event's menu and choose "Remove" to delete just that event. In a group's member list, open a member's menu and choose "Remove" to delete that person with their wishlists and note. If they were already part of a draw, only their name stays, so that draw still adds up. And in a group you take part in, you can empty your wishlist or your note for your Secret Santa. For an online group, each of these takes effect on my servers right away. If you can't find how to delete something, email me at info@circletools.ch and I'll sort it out.

data.name: Legal_Delete_WhatBody
data.value: Everything tied to your account is deleted. People you added to a Circle as managed profiles stay, because they belong to the Circle rather than to you, and the other members still rely on them. What you wrote in someone else's group — your wishlist, your note for your Secret Santa — stays in that group, because it's part of their draw. If you'd rather it didn't, empty it before you go.

data.name: Legal_Delete_RetentionBody
data.value: When you delete your account or a single thing, it's gone from the app straight away — I can't bring it back, and neither can you. The one exception is my encrypted backups, which I keep only in case something goes badly wrong: deleted data can remain in an older backup for up to about six months before it's deleted for good. I never restore a backup to bring deleted data back, only after a real outage. Emails I sent you are deleted from my server at the latest 7 days after sending.

data.name: Legal_Delete_LocalBody
data.value: Without an account, a group kept on your device exists only there. You remove it by deleting it in the app, or by clearing the app's data in your browser or phone settings. That data never reached me. A group you put online without an account, or opened through someone's link, is on my servers: delete it or leave it in the app. A group that no account owns is also removed automatically after a year without any activity.

data.name: Legal_Delete_ContactBody
data.value: If you can't get into your account to delete it, email me at info@circletools.ch and I'll help you.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_AboutBody
data.value: I'm a software engineer and build CircleTools in my free time. It started with Secret Santa, an app for my own family's gift exchange — I couldn't find one that did what we needed. More apps for families and groups of friends are meant to follow. The app is free, and I hope it makes your get-togethers a little easier.
